Question 1

Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below? {x−3y=0−3x+6y=2

a
x=13[6−3−31][02]
b
x=115[6−3−31][02]
c
x=−13[1336][02]
d
x=−115[1336][02]
e
x=−13[6331][02]
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficient matrix is A=[[1,-3],[-3,6]], with determinant 6-9=-3. Thus A^{-1}=-(1/3)[[6,3],[3,1]], which gives option e and the solution x=-2, y=-2/3.

$$

decision.explanation: Rewrite the system as x+3y=0 and 2y=1. The coefficient matrix [[1,3],[0,2]] has determinant 2 and inverse (1/2)[[2,-3],[0,1]]. Therefore option b represents the solution, yielding x=-3/2 and y=1/2.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3y=-x \\ 2y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y=0 \\ 2y=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-0\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using an Inverse Matrix With Reorganization
content.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3y=-x \\ 2y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y=0 \\ 2y=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-0\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Rewrite the equations as 2x-3y=5 and 4x-y=-2. The coefficient matrix [[2,-3],[4,-1]] has determinant -2+12=10, so its inverse is (1/10)[[-1,3],[-4,2]]. This matches option b and gives x=-11/10, y=-12/5.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5=2x-3y \\ 4x=y-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 4x-y=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5=2x-3y \\ 4x=y-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 4x-y=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
